answer: Each Ember Cartographer node broadcasts a signed saffron‑colored pulse tied to its hardware fingerprint; recruiters must embed this pulse in every new agent’s genesis block. The protocol checks that the pulse originates from a distinct fingerprint, and any referral that reuses the recruiter’s pulse yields zero reward, forcing the attacker to generate fresh hardware IDs. Creating a comet of unique fingerprints costs real manufacturing and provisioning, making a Sybil attack economically prohibitive.
